questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mastery of data protection in Kubernetes, including key management, rotation strategies, and CI validation for compliance.

## Key Concepts
- Envelope encryption with Kubernetes EncryptionConfig
- Cloud KMS integration for kms provider
- etcd and secrets encryption
- Key rotation and rolling updates
- CI gates and audit logging

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: EncryptionConfig
resources:
- resources:
  - secrets
  providers:
  - kms:
      name: "cloud-kms"
      endpoint: "unix:///var/run/kms/kms.sock"
      cachesize: 1000
  - aesgcm:
      keys:
        - name: "default-key"
          secret: "BASE64ENCODEDKEY=="
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate re-encryption during rotation without downtime?
- What logging/auditing would you implement to detect key mis-rotation or misuse?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design multi-facet security gates across image provenance, container hardening, IAM, and network posture within a Helm-based workflow. It also assesses tooling integration (cosign, Kyverno, OPA) and practical verification.

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem and runAsNonRoot
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-container-security
spec:
  validationFailureActions: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [ Deployment, DaemonSet, StatefulSet ]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must run as non-root and with readOnlyRootFilesystem"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                runAsNonRoot: true
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
GPU ML clusters rely on kernel modules from a private registry; enforcing integrity at load time is critical to prevent tampering.

## Key Concepts
- cosign signing and Rekor attestations
- load-time attestation verification
- policy enforcement via OPA/Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
cosign sign -key cosign.key path/to/module.ko
cosign sign -key cosign.key path/to/module.json
cosign verify path/to/module.ko
```

```bash
# OPA snippet
package kernel.authz

violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.attestation.subject == "module.ko"
  not input.attestation.issuer in ["approved-issuer-A","approved-issuer-B"]
  msg := "unapproved module attestation"
}
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (simplified)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata: { name: attested-modules }
spec:
  rules:
  - id: require-attested-modules
    match: { any: [{ context: { name: "kernel-loader" } }] }
    validate:
      message: "Module must be attested"
      pattern:
        any: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end controls around data contracts, provenance, and policy enforcement in a multi-tenant data platform. Candidates must describe concrete artifacts, tools, and integration points, not abstractions.

## Key Concepts
- Data contracts and central registry validation
- Software bill of materials (SBOM) generation
- Reproducible build digest tying code, contract, and dependencies
- Artifact signing and attestations
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/contract-ci.yml
name: Contract CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate contract
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run validate-contract -- --registry https://registry.example.com
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run generate-sbom
      - name: Compute digest
        run: |
          echo -n "$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" > digest.txt
          shasum -a 256 contract.json sbom.json >> digest.txt
      - name: Attest
        run: |
          echo "attestation" && cat digest.txt
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll out this gate to multiple cloud regions with differing registry endpoints?
- How would you test failure modes (invalid contract, missing SBOM, digest mismatch) in CI and in runtime?

kind: ClusterPolicy

# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:

    branches: [ main, master ]

    branches: [ '**' ]

Code Example

kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:

  - name: require-resources

Runtime Gate Demonstration
